dex.text: Sits in the chalk like a raisin in a bun until a storm prises it loose. Strike it and it sparks, so please don't.
dex.fact: Flint forms as hard nodules inside chalk, from the silica of ancient sponges. Struck against steel it throws sparks, and Sussex and Kent builders split it to face cottages and churches.

dex.text: Stands on the clifftop looking out to sea, as it has for longer than anyone remembers. Takes nothing on trust, especially weather from France.
dex.fact: The White Cliffs of Dover are chalk, built up from the tiny limy plates of sea algae called coccolithophores, laid down on a warm sea floor between about 100 and 66 million years ago.
